dedupe_keys.name: brazil and us data centre infrastructure geospatial preparation workflow

description: This Python project prepares geospatial features for data-centre siting studies in Brazil and the United States. Its README describes facility-location cleaning, address geocoding, cell-tower density within several radii, distance to substations and transmission lines, and census-tract prediction examples for São Paulo. The public tree contains source scripts, notebooks and processed CSV or GeoJSON examples. A modeller could adapt the preparation code to assemble candidate-site features or examine how facilities relate to power and communications infrastructure. The project’s facility list began with a scrape of datacenters.com, and some Brazilian coordinates were manually chosen using Google Maps after automated geocoding failed. Those source rights and location accuracies were not verified, so this draft does not license or endorse the processed facility tables as a standalone dataset. This review did not open the repository’s .env file, download inputs, execute scripts or assess model predictions. GitHub metadata reports MIT for the project code. Geographic coverage is partial and depends on the included inputs. Related resources are the original commercial and public infrastructure sources. Its simulation use is constructing candidate facility locations and power or telecom proximity features for siting scenarios, not forecasting actual future builds.
licence: MIT for repository code; scraped commercial facility data, geocoded coordinates and third-party infrastructure layers retain separate unverified rights.
